_how_to_apply: 1. Append/patch `proposed_records[]` where each `collection` says, in the order given - artifacts FIRST (the routes and the publication reference them, so applying a route first leaves the build red between steps), then publications, then routes.

2. ⛔ MIRROR `grade` AND `closure_note` INTO THE LEGACY REGISTRY IN THE SAME COMMIT - see `_the_second_home_that_must_be_updated_with_it` below. MEASURED, not guessed: applying the graph patches alone produces SEVEN `[L3]` errors.

3. Regenerate BOTH generated views: `python3 systems/systems_check.py --write-views` AND `python3 research/manuscripts/emc_systems_map_check.py --write-view`. Both trees are GENERATED and a hand-edit fails the build; the second is easy to forget and was the only error left standing in the validation run below.

5. `python3 research/manuscripts/lint_claims.py` - `what_it_would_claim` and every route `grade.value` are linted through systems/views/**, so a claim written one notch too strong fails CI rather than a review.

6. ⚠ DEDUPE FIRST: `ART-EMC-EXPRESSION-PANELS` below registers research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json, which the fusion-transcriptional-output session is also reading today. If that session proposes the same artifact, APPLY ONE, not both - a second registration is a second home for the same fact.

_the_second_home_that_must_be_updated_wi.what: `systems/graph/routes.json` and `research/manuscripts/emc-systems-map.json` BOTH carry a route's `grade` and `closure_note`, and `systems_check.check_legacy_agreement` fails the build on any disagreement (`SHARED_ROUTE_FIELDS`). The graph is the source; the legacy file is a policed projection that eleven consumers still read.
_the_second_home_that_must_be_updated_wi.and_these_are_graph_only: `readiness` and `remaining_unknowns` are NOT in SHARED_ROUTE_FIELDS - the graph adds them and the legacy file has no counterpart to disagree with. Copying them into the legacy registry would CREATE the duplication this check exists to prevent.
_the_second_home_that_must_be_updated_wi.publications_and_artifacts: Neither collection is mirrored. PUB-SURFACE-TARGETS and the two ART-* records are graph-only.

proposed_records.note: ⚠ See _how_to_apply step 5 - another session may propose this same record today.

record.what_it_is: Targeted gene and curated-panel reads in the two READABLE EMC array series - GSE24369 on GPL6244 (6 EMC vs 29 comparator sarcomas) and GSE4303 on GPL3290 (10 vs 6). Nine reads; read_8_SURFACE_ANTIGEN is the surface-antigen one, and it carries a per-gene cross_platform_board over 100 genes.
record.control_note: reads.control reads NR4A3, ENO3 and MKI67 - two genes that must be up and one that must be flat - on these exact platforms before any antigen is read. A control licenses reading the other rows and nothing more.
limits: Two platforms with different physics; GPL3290 is two-colour log-ratio against a reference pool, so an absolute level there is not a statement that a gene is expressed.
Different comparator arms between the two series, so a single-platform move is a lead and not a replication.
Bulk archival tissue, not deconvolved - a stromal or matrix antigen can read high because the compartment is present.
No multiple-testing correction anywhere, by design; every t and df is reported.
READABILITY IS AN INSTRUMENT STATE, NEVER A LOW READING. Genes unreadable on a platform carry READABLE_ON_ONE_PLATFORM_ONLY or NOT_READABLE_ON_EITHER_PLATFORM and must never be reported as negative.

record.what_it_is: The ONLY deposit reachable at $0 that carries EMC libraries alongside NORMAL tissue. 19 genes, n = 4 EMC, 27 normal-organ libraries and 32 non-EMC sarcoma libraries on 3SEQ. Its canonical interpretation is research/manuscripts/gse28866-tumour-vs-normal-reading.md, which is canonical_for it.
record.control_note: NR4A3 is detected in the EMC arm and its median across the 32 other sarcomas is zero - the fusion's own 3' partner behaving as the disease definition requires, in a cohort this repository did not choose. A control, not a result.
limits: n = 4 EMC. Medians of four libraries: no confidence interval, no test, no distribution.
3' end read density is NOT array intensity and must NEVER be pooled with GPL6244/GPL3290.
Several genes rest on a SINGLE PEAK - CSPG4, FAP, GPC3, L1CAM, PRAME among them; n_peaks is in the artifact for this reason.

TWO AXES, NEVER ONE. The 27 normals are visceral organs with almost no soft tissue in them, so the normal arm is an on-target/off-tumour EXPOSURE axis and NOT a lineage-specificity axis; the 32-sarcoma arm is the lineage axis. Reading either as the other is the error this artifact's reading memo exists to prevent.
The normals are a tissue panel, not matched adjacent tissue, and six organs are not a body.
Transcript only. No protein, no surface localisation, no safety statement, no therapeutic-window statement.

fields.what_it_would_claim: A surface-antigen search built on a lineage surrogate and a normal-tissue prior does not transfer to the disease it was built for: checked against three EMC tumour cohorts on three platform families, NOT ONE of the eleven therapeutic addresses this work's routes name is concordantly elevated in EMC relative to comparator sarcomas, ZERO of the eight surrogate-selective antigens are concordantly elevated on both arrays, and the one antigen that IS elevated on both - ALCAM, which no route names - shows no separation from normal visceral organ tissue on the only cohort able to measure that. The surrogate's NEGATIVES transferred and its POSITIVES did not, which is a caution that applies to every surrogate-based rare-tumour target list. ⚠ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-07, RETAINED: the prior claim was that every negative is 'bounded by that surrogate basis rather than by an EMC tissue measurement', from 'one cell line and a translocation-sarcoma comparison set' - the tissue measurement now exists and the bound is discharged.

proposed_records.note: Grade OWNER is research/manuscripts/emc-surface-target-landscape.md, so this route's grade sentence is the manuscript's to move and this is the record that must follow it. TIER UNCHANGED - see _what_was_deliberately_NOT_proposed.

grade.value: Tier 3 - already red-teamed in this repo, and now checked against EMC tumour tissue. ⚠ THE TWO ANTIGENS STILL FAIL DIFFERENTLY: B7-H3/CD276 is NOT selective in the surrogate (BH q = 1.0, enrichment 0.14) and is LOWER in EMC than in comparator sarcomas on the one array platform that can read it, while sitting mid-to-high in that array's own distribution - expressed and not differential. CD56/NCAM1 IS selective in the surrogate (q = 0.0, enrichment 1.74), reads FLAT_ON_BOTH arrays in EMC tissue, and fails on the normal-tissue / immune window (NK cells) with a discontinued CD56 ADC precedent.

readiness.why_not_higher: The negative is now measured on BOTH a surrogate and EMC tumour tissue and the two agree in direction, which is stronger than either alone - but both are transcript, and B7-H3's clinical traction rests on protein being tumour-restricted despite broad mRNA. A transcript negative cannot close a protein question.
missing: a protein-level measurement on EMC tissue

remaining_unknowns: Whether B7-H3 PROTEIN on EMC tissue behaves like the transcript. This is the whole remaining question, and it is the one the transcript negative cannot answer.
⛔ CD276 is NOT READABLE on GPL3290, so the EMC-tissue reading rests on ONE array platform and one probe. An absent reading is not a reading of absence.
fields.closure_note: The selectivity premise was MEASURED and failed FOR B7-H3 in the surrogate (BH q = 1.0), and the EMC-tissue read agrees in direction on the one platform that can take it. ⚠ It did NOT fail for CD56 - NCAM1 returns q = 0.0 and is selectivity-significant in the surrogate; what fails there is the normal-tissue window (VITAL_OR_IMMUNE_LIABILITY, NK cells), and in EMC tissue NCAM1 is flat on both arrays. Collapsing the two into one 'not selective' verdict was wrong for half this route and still is.

remaining_unknowns: ⚠ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-07: 'Whether the stromal target is present in EMC's particular myxoid matrix - this has never been measured.' FAP is now read in EMC tumour tissue on both array platforms and is FLAT_ON_BOTH against comparator sarcomas, and the whole 13-gene stromal/matrix panel is LOWER in EMC on both. ⚠ Read the comparator before reading the result: GSE24369's comparators are desmoid fibromatosis and fibrosarcoma - fibroblastic lesions in which FAP is expected to be high - and EMC itself sits high in that array's own distribution. This does NOT say EMC lacks FAP; it says a FAP-directed route cannot claim EMC as a selectively FAP-rich indication among soft-tissue tumours.
⛔ Bulk archival tissue cannot separate the tumour compartment from the stroma, so neither the negative nor a positive would attribute the signal. A single-cell or spatial EMC dataset is what would.

The surfaceome screen (ART-SURFACE-EXPRESSION) returns FAP selectivity_q = 0.1555 / myxoid 0.0 - but it is DepMap tumour-cell MONOCULTURE with no CAF compartment (surfaceome-instrument-limits.json L1/L2/L5, demonstrated at frac_expressed 0.0 for LRRC15), so it cannot see the stroma this route targets and never answered the question. That its direction happens to agree with the tissue read is a coincidence of direction, not a corroboration.
Whether a stromal-targeted radioligand delivers enough dose to the tumour cells.
fields.closure_note: No longer 'emerging and unmeasured in EMC' - it is emerging and measured unfavourably at transcript level, on an instrument that cannot attribute the signal to a compartment.

_flagged_for_trimcrae_not_proposed.the_decision_that_is_not_mine: Either (a) split the blocker into functional-genomics vs expression, or (b) leave it and let the publication's own claim carry the distinction. Splitting a blocker changes what every other route inheriting it means, which is a program-level call.
